findings.where: digests/2026-11-16-v2.md lines 58-65: "with your V2 tokens as Figma holds them ... All 24 measured page states pass text contrast and control-edge contrast" and the "V2 as given" column
findings.problem: The "as given" screens are not built from the tokens Figma holds. Their token file is built with --no-overrides but still merges the repo's proposed tokens, and the bridge maps every control edge to the proposed border/strong (3.24 to 1). Figma's only edge token is border/primary at 1.35 to 1, which the same summary lists as a harm. So the owner is shown their direction passing a check it fails, and the "honest result" that as-given and merged look the same is partly produced by this.
findings.evidence: v2/screens/bridge.css: `--sv-color-edge: var(--color-border-strong)`, plus --size-control-lg, --border-width-sm, --border-ring-width, --duration-fast. `grep -n border-strong v2/screens/tokens-as-given/tokens.css` -> line 242 `--color-border-strong: #8c8f97`. v2/screens/measurements.json: as-given lowestControl 3.24, identical to merged. v2/tools/build-compare.mjs line 8: built by `build-tokens.mjs --no-overrides`. v2/screens/index.html line 38 says "exactly as Figma holds them today".
findings.fix: Either rebuild B with no proposed tokens (edge on border/primary, Figma's own sizes) and re-measure, or relabel B as "Figma's values plus the proposed tokens, without the contrast fixes" and say the control-edge pass comes from a token Figma does not have. Rewrite the "honest result" paragraph to match.

findings.where: ds-components/src/dialog/dialog.extensions.css (header and footer flex-shrink: 0, content and overlay overflow visible); test dialog-body-scrolls in ds-components/src/dialog/dialog.tests.mjs:588
findings.problem: With text at 200 percent (root font size 200%, the same method input.tests.mjs uses) the Dialog loses its actions on common phone sizes. Header and footer never shrink, so the body collapses to 0 px and the footer spills out of the dialog and below the screen; the page is scroll-locked and neither overlay nor content scrolls. In the not-dismissible example this traps a touch user: no action is visible, Escape and the overlay press are blocked. It becomes a release blocker the moment a Dialog ships. The MUST dialog-body-scrolls ("footer with the actions stay fully visible") is tested at 100% text only.
findings.evidence: node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chaitanyalandge-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-ebabe688-c813-4d37-95fc-498a492cc12d-5e00ea11-9ff3-4643-b571-765ec27a06ab-scratch-2026-11-13-02c7be/b28519ae-d5a9-4657-800a-f0c0e2b58dcd/scratchpad/review/break-components/sizes200.mjs -> default 360x640: bodyHeight 0, "Use this address: cut by the screen edge"; not-dismissible 360x640: bodyHeight 0, "Use a different card: cut", "I have confirmed it: wholly below the screen"; not-dismissible 375x667: second action wholly below; confirm-step 360x640: "Add express delivery: wholly below". All fit only from 390x844. dialogfit.mjs in the same folder: default 320x568 at 200%: content 32-536, header 33-473, body 473-473, footer 473-893, overlay overflow visible, pageScrollable false. Also at 100% in a 320x256 viewport (1280x1024 zoomed 400%) confirm-step: body 141-141 (0 px), footer 141-277 against content 16-240. Screenshot: shots/dialogfit-not-dismissible-320x568-text-200-.png shows title and description only.
findings.fix: When header plus footer exceed the box, let the whole content scroll (for example overflow-y auto on the content with a minimum block size on the body, or overflow on the overlay). Add 200% text cases at 360x640 and a 320x256 case to dialog-body-scrolls and dialog-not-dismissible-has-way-out; until fixed, list it in the summary's not-proven section.

findings.where: ds-components/src/button/button.tsx:98-105 and 149 (handleClick merged through Radix Slot); test button-disabled-inert and button-loading-inert in button.tests.mjs
findings.problem: With asChild, disabled or loading does not stop the child's own onClick: Slot runs the child's handler first and Button's guard second. A router link that navigates in its own onClick would still navigate (inferred from the measured order; no router was run). The tests have no asChild disabled or loading case, so removing the asChild-disabled guard entirely still passes.
findings.evidence: probe1.mjs "button asChild + disabled (link)": attributes aria-disabled true, tabIndex 0; "after Enter: events [child.onClick]", "after click: events [child.onClick]"; same for asChild + loading. Mutation run: node .../break-components/mutate.mjs button-aschild -> "SURVIVED button-aschild-disabled-not-inert -> test:button-disabled-inert; baseline: passed; mutated: passed" (bundle line "const inert = loading || asChild && disabled;" replaced by "const inert = loading;").
findings.fix: Block in the capture phase when inert (onClickCapture: preventDefault and stopPropagation) so the child's handler never runs; add as-link disabled and as-link loading examples and assert the child's handler count.

findings.where: ds-components/src/tabs/tabs.tsx:139-142 and 154-160; ds-components/src/dialog/dialog.tsx:63-66, 184-191, 292-298 (setRef)
findings.problem: TabsList, DialogContent and DialogBody mishandle React 19 callback refs that return a cleanup function: the cleanup is never called and the callback is called again with null. A ref written the React 19 way (observe the node, return disconnect) leaks, or throws on unmount when it uses the null. findings.where: v2/tools/contrast-pairs.json 'exempt'; digest table row 'Pairs exempt, each with a reason (disabled, dividers)'
findings.problem: 28 of the 52 are sound: WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 both exclude inactive components. The 16 'divider' pairs are not an exemption in WCAG; a line is out of scope only while it is not needed to identify a control. Eight of them are border/primary/hover and border/primary/active, tokens with interactive states, which cannot be 'a line that only divides content'. The remaining 8 are focus-ring-beside-fills, 'reported only', which the digest's parenthesis omits. The focus-ring reasoning holds for the five components: every ring uses ring/offset 2px except forced-colours menu items.
findings.evidence: Committed audit: exempt by rule {disabled: 28, dividers: 16, focus-ring-beside-fills: 8}. Specs: outlineOffset is ring/offset on Button, Input, Tabs and Dialog; 'none' only under media forced-colors in dropdown-menu.spec.json styles[7-9]. border/primary/default is used only by the menu separator; border/primary/hover and /active are used by no spec.
findings.fix: Rename the group to 'not a control edge' with the condition stated, move border/primary/hover and /active to a 'not used by any component, unmeasured' list, and name all three groups in the digest.

findings.where: ds-components/src/dialog/dialog.css rules for [data-state="closed"] on dialog-content and dialog-overlay; dialog.spec.json
findings.problem: Two generated rules can never have a visible effect. They shorten a transition on the closed state, but no animation is defined and Radix removes a closed dialog at once, so the state lasts zero frames. The base transition on overlay and content does nothing for the same reason, so duration/base ('a menu or dialog appearing or leaving') is not yet used in effect. Dialog and menu also set no z-index (no layer token), so they depend on DOM order under any app header that has one.
findings.evidence: dialog.extensions.css line 4: 'No animation: the fade and scale are not carried yet.' grep animation|keyframes|forceMount in ds-components/src/dialog: none in CSS; forceMount is omitted from the props types. grep z-index in ds-components/src: no match.
findings.fix: Remove the two closed-state rules until an exit animation exists, or add the keyframes so Radix keeps the node mounted. Propose a layer token for overlays.
